touched_source.description: Complete touched file source at the reviewed revision; preserve executable bodies and test assertions. The source bank defaults to diff plus touched files.

gemfile_diff.description: Gemfile dependency changes for this review.

siblings.description: Two or three deterministically selected sibling files doing a comparable job in the same layer, directory, superclass, or concern. Record selection and omissions.

volatile_dependencies.description: Woods volatile_dependencies report with 365-day commit counts, configured ratio (default 3.0), and skipped dependencies under five commits. Absent or disabled enrichment is unknown, not stability.

similar_code_search.description: Repository search results for similar existing logic, with searched scope and revision.

change_kind_fix.description: An independently supplied premise that this is a bug fix, with the intended regression behavior. The parallel change_kind answer is not evidence available to this question.

schema.description: Schema evidence including columns, indexes and constraints, corresponding to schema.rb for the reviewed revision.

pr_description.description: The supplied pull request description or an explicit empty description for a known existing review.

database_configuration.description: Relevant database.yml topology with secrets removed; writer and replica configuration.

locale_usage.description: Evidence of whether the app uses locales and surrounding translation conventions.

queue_adapter.description: BehavioralProfile queue adapter and relevant job framework (Sidekiq-native versus Active Job).

rails_version.description: Exact Rails version for the reviewed application.

callers.description: Caller source relevant to every touched method, column, constant, and route. Relationship metadata alone does not establish complete caller bodies or scope.

reference_search.description: Repository grep/reference results for every touched method, column, constant, and route, with searched scope and revision.

commit_messages.description: Commit messages for the reviewed change.

changelog_policy.description: Evidence of whether this repository maintains a changelog or release notes and its applicable entry convention.

local_helper_search.description: Repository search for equivalent helpers, concerns, and base classes, with searched scope and revision.

source.description: Source: Rails Doctrine, *Getting Real*, the "Majestic Monolith" and "vanilla Rails" posts. Lens: convention over configuration, conceptual compression, ceremony is a cost.

sections.name: Views
sections.title: Views and Hotwire — DHH, the HTML-over-the-wire half

source.description: Source: thoughtbot Rails guide, Rails style guide, Hotwire handbook and pattern guides. Kept separate from the framework-conformance section so each bar measures one thing. Runs on views, partials, helpers, components, and Stimulus controllers in the diff.

sections.name: Metz
sections.title: Sandi Metz — will this hurt when it changes?

source.description: Source: *POODR* ch. 2–8, *99 Bottles of OOP*, "The Wrong Abstraction". Lens: dependency direction, message-based design, cost of change.

Source: *POODR* ch. 9, "Magic Tricks of Testing"; Justin Searls (*How to Stop Hating Your Tests*, *Please Don't Mock Me*); Vladimir Dementyev and Evil Martians (TestProf, flaky-test series). Lens: test incoming messages for state, outgoing commands for being sent, nothing else; and a test suite is a design signal and a feedback loop, not a ritual. Runs on the test files in the diff.

sections.name: Berkopec
sections.title: Nate Berkopec — will this be slow, and do we know?

source.description: Source: *The Complete Guide to Rails Performance*, Speedshop blog. Lens: measure before optimizing, the database is usually the problem, the request path is sacred.

sections.name: Uchitelle
sections.title: Eileen Uchitelle — will this break the database?

source.description: Source: Rails core work on multi-DB, connection handling, and upgrades; Andrew Kane's strong\_migrations for the migration rules. Lens: the database outlives the code, constraints belong in the schema.

sections.name: Batsov
sections.title: Bozhidar Batsov — Rails style guide semantics

source.description: Source: the community Rails style guide and rubocop-rails, plus the thoughtbot Rails guide. Nearly every row has a cop. They stay in because the cop fires on syntax and the question asks whether the shortcut was intended; cop-versus-Jev disagreement is the calibration signal.

sections.name: Avdi
sections.title: Avdi Grimm — can this method be trusted?

source.description: Source: *Confident Ruby*, *Exceptional Ruby*. Lens: collect input, perform work, deliver output, handle failure — in that order; nil is not a value.

sections.name: tenderlove
sections.title: tenderlove — what does this cost the VM?

source.description: Source: Aaron Patterson's talks and blog on allocation, GC, and ActiveRecord internals. Lens: objects are not free, memory bloat is a slow leak.

sections.name: Security
sections.title: Security — Justin Collins / Rails Security Guide

source.description: Source: Brakeman (Justin Collins), the official Rails Security Guide, OWASP Top 10. Lens: every input is hostile, every record lookup needs an owner, every dynamic dispatch is an injection point. Brakeman covers some of these statically; the rest need semantics.

sections.name: Perham
sections.title: Mike Perham — background jobs and concurrency

source.description: Source: Sidekiq best practices and wiki. Lens: jobs run twice, run late, run out of order, and run against a database that has moved on.

sections.name: Observability
sections.title: Observability — can you debug it at 3am?

source.description: Source: Rails error reporter and structured event guides, Semantic Logger and Lograge write-ups, Sidekiq docs. No persona on the council owned this; Charity Majors' framing is borrowed for the question. Runs on rescue blocks, log calls, raises, and job definitions in the diff.

sections.name: Codebase
sections.title: The codebase — does this look like it belongs here?

source.description: No persona. The reviewer is the repo itself. State must carry two or three sibling files from the same layer doing a comparable job (same directory, same superclass, or same concern), chosen deterministically. This is the cheapest context to pack and the one most likely to catch an agent drifting from house style.

sections.name: Rollout
sections.title: Rollout — can we ship and unship this?

source.description: No persona. Lens: the deploy and the migration are separate events, and the previous version of the code is still running for a while.

sections.name: Blast

source.description: No persona. Distinct from `metz_blast_radius`, which measures cost of change; this measures reach into data other code depends on. State must carry callers and references found by grep for every method, column, constant, and route the diff touches.
